newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar finishes lower on year-end demand.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar finishes lower on year-end demand.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed lower against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday on late year-end U.S. dollar buying from local importers, dealers said.
The local dollar closed at T$27.501 against Tuesday's T$27.493 end. Turnover through dealers was US$134 million, sharply higher from Tuesday's US$54.5 million.
"Some US$51 million of turnover emerged during the last 30 minutes, mostly from importers who needed American currency to meet their year-end commercial demand," said one dealer.

The Taiwan dollar rate hovered in a narrow range throughout most of the session despite renewed buying in Taiwan's stock market that was triggered in part by a Wall Street stock picker's bullishness on emerging markets.
Brokers said today's active stock buying failed to fuel demand for the Taiwan dollar as many foreign fund managers have started their Christmas vacations.
A narrow T$27.49-27.51 range was seen for Thursday.
